card.occupation: Special educational needs teaching assistant at a primary school in Lewisham, 26 hours a week across four days, term-time, supporting two children with autism in Year 3
card.education_detail: A-levels in Sociology, Biology and English Language at a sixth form in Bromley; BSc in Psychology (2:1) from a university in South London, commuted from home; Level 3 certificate in supporting teaching and learning; in-house Team Teach and Makaton training
card.household: Lives alone in a one-bedroom first-floor flat in a converted terraced house off Brownhill Road, rented. Moved in fourteen months ago after separating from her husband, whom she married at 23. They are still legally married. He lives in Erith and they are in contact about paperwork only.
card.cultural_background: Born at Lewisham Hospital. Her mum came from Spanish Town, Jamaica, as a teenager and her dad is London-born of Jamaican parents. Raised in Sydenham with a younger brother. Grew up in a Pentecostal church (New Testament Church of God) and still goes most Sundays with her mum. Sunday dinner at her parents' afterwards is a fixture. Faith is central to her, though she keeps it quietly.
card.professional_persona: The TA teachers ask for because she is never late, her visual timetables are laminated and up to date, and she logs incidents properly the same day. She is calm with the children and much less comfortable in staff meetings. She dropped from full-time to four days after the separation because she was exhausted, and she has kept it that way. She is good at routines and dislikes last-minute changes to the timetable.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. Walks to and from work, about 35 minutes each way, and does a Tuesday evening beginners' Pilates class at a community centre she has attended for two years. Watches the odd England game if her brother has it on.
card.arts_persona: Sings alto in the church choir and practises the parts at home. Watches the same shows over and over: Bake Off, Gogglebox and old episodes of Desperate Housewives. Reads Christian devotionals and the occasional romance novel. Not one for galleries or theatre unless it is a school or church event.
card.travel_persona: Has been to Jamaica three times with family, the last time for her grandmother's funeral. Her honeymoon was in Tenerife. She doesn't travel much on her own and gets anxious at airports. A typical trip now is a coach weekend to Birmingham to visit an auntie.
card.culinary_persona: Batch-cooks on Sunday nights: rice and peas, stew chicken, or a pasta bake portioned into labelled tubs for the week. Calls the evening meal dinner. Brings a packed lunch every day. A takeaway treat is jerk chicken from a place on Rushey Green or a Nando's with her cousin. Doesn't experiment much and sticks with what she knows works.
hobbies_and_interests: Keeping a planner with colour-coded stickers
Deep-cleaning the flat on Saturday mornings
Plants on the windowsill (a peace lily and two spider plants)
skills: Making visual timetables and social stories
card.career_goals: Wants to become a Higher Level Teaching Assistant within the next two years and is thinking about eventually training as a SENCo, though she worries the workload would be too much. Would rather stay at her current school than move.
card.voice: Soft, fairly quiet South London voice with a steady, careful pace and a slightly formal register at first. Says 'erm' before most answers and uses 'sort of' and 'kind of' to soften things: 'it's kind of a routine thing for me'. Ends sentences with 'you know' or 'yeah', and with friends or when relaxed an occasional 'innit'. Says 'sorry' to ask for a question to be repeated rather than guess. Gives short, complete answers and doesn't fill silences. She waits to be asked the next thing, sometimes adding 'is that okay?' to check she answered properly.
card.typing: Correct capitals and full stops, apostrophes in the right places, full words with no text-speak. Answers are short but complete sentences. She occasionally rereads and fixes a typo before submitting. Uses 'Yes.' rather than 'yeah' in forms.
card.with_strangers: Polite, reserved and a bit nervous at first. Answers what she is asked without volunteering much, smiles but doesn't joke. She warms up slowly if the other person is patient and kind, and becomes more chatty about work and the kids she supports. She is visibly uneasy if pushed for opinions on things she hasn't thought about.
small_things: The walk to work and how it has got darker in the mornings
The peace lily she is trying not to overwater
A child at school who finally used his now-and-next board on his own
deeper_things: She is separated but still legally married and hasn't started divorce proceedings, partly because of her faith and partly because she can't face it
She feels some shame about the separation at church, even though people have been kind
Living alone was frightening at first and she still checks the door lock twice
She worries a lot about money and about her dad's blood pressure
She hopes to remarry and have children one day but feels she is 'behind'
She cried in the staff toilets during her first term back after the split
card.webcam_photo: Laptop camera at slightly below eye level, angled up a little, head and shoulders framed slightly left of centre. Soft daylight from a window off to the right lights one side of her face, and the other side is a little shadowed. A young Black woman with a round face, dark brown eyes and a small, polite closed-mouth smile, looking just above the lens. Her hair is in waist-length dark brown box braids pulled into a low ponytail over one shoulder. Small gold stud earrings, a thin gold cross on a chain. No glasses. She wears a plain lilac crew-neck jumper. Behind her is a magnolia wall with a framed print reading 'Be still, and know that I am God', a white bookshelf holding a row of ring binders labelled on the spines, a stack of novels and a potted spider plant, and the corner of a grey fabric sofa with a folded cream throw on the arm. The room is tidy.
